title: Do these runs agree across devices?

blocks.text: A routing team solves the same LP on laptops (CPU only), on a build server, and on a GPU workstation, and keeps a record of each run: the `device` (`"cpu"` or `"gpu"`), the `solver`, the `objective`, and a `digest` of the solution's bits. Before a release they want one function that says whether a set of runs agrees, by a rule written down once:

items: one CPU run is the reference: the first CPU run in the list. With no CPU run there is no reference, and the result is exactly `["no CPU reference"]`: no other check runs, so not even a repeat that differs is reported until a CPU run is added;
runs of the same solver on the same device are repeats, and a repeat must give the same digest and objective as that pair's first run, else `"<device>/<solver>: repeat differs"`;
every run's objective must be within `tol` of the reference's, relatively (divided by $`\max(1, \lvert\text{reference}\rvert)`$), else `"<device>/<solver>: off the reference"`.

blocks.text: Write `check_runs(runs, tol)` in `runs.py`, returning the problems sorted, each once; an empty list means the runs agree. One test, `test_real_runs_on_this_machine_agree_and_a_run_off_by_a_thousandth_is_caught`, solves a small LP with `highspy` on this machine; on the GPU image with a GPU it adds two GPU PDLP runs. On a machine without a GPU that test runs its CPU part only, and it says nothing about the GPU part: no test is reported as skipped. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from runs import check_runs


def run(device, solver, objective, digest):
    return {"device": device, "solver": solver, "objective": objective, "digest": digest}


agree = [run("cpu", "simplex", 250.0, "aa11"), run("cpu", "ipm", 250.0000001, "bb22"),
         run("gpu", "pdlp", 250.00002, "cc33"), run("gpu", "pdlp", 250.00002, "cc33")]
print("four runs near 250, tol 1e-6:", check_runs(agree, 1e-6))
print("same runs, tol 1e-8:", check_runs(agree, 1e-8))
print("a pdlp repeat with another digest:", check_runs(agree + [run("gpu", "pdlp", 250.00002, "dd44")], 1e-6))
print("gpu runs only:", check_runs(agree[2:], 1e-6))

from __future__ import annotations


def check_runs(runs: list[dict], tol: float) -> list[str]:
    """Problems with a set of runs of one LP on several devices; an empty list means they agree.

    A run is {"device": "cpu" | "gpu", "solver": str, "objective": float, "digest": str}.
    """
    # TODO: a CPU reference, repeats held to equal bits, every run within tol of the reference.
    return ["not checked"]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(check_runs([{"device": "cpu", "solver": "ipm", "objective": 10.0, "digest": "a"}], 1e-6))

cases.says: real runs on this machine agree, and a run off by a thousandth is caught
a repeat of one solver on one device that changed is caught
different solvers or devices are compared within tolerance, not by bits
the tolerance is relative to the objective's size
with no CPU run there is no reference to compare with

origin.section: The Same Answer Means Within a Stated Tolerance

concepts: answers from different devices are compared within a relative tolerance, repeats by their bits
